title: Exploring multi-parameter optimization in FRG
authors: A. Codello, G. P. Vacca, D. Zarrilli
abstract: The use of nonperturbative Wilsonian functional renormalization group (FRG) equations within an unavoidable approximation scheme produces physical results that depend on the choice of the coarse-graining regulator. This dependence of physical observables on the regulator can be minimized according to the principle of minimal sensitivity (PMS). For the 1PI formulation based on the Wetterich-Morris equation, we propose to investigate the optimal choice within a space of compactly supported polynomial regulators parametrized by a set of variables. We test this approach using the derivative expansion of the effective average action up to fourth order, applying it to the scalar field theory representing the three-dimensional Ising universality class and minimizing the dependence of the anomalous dimension on the regulator. At fourth order, we find appreciable corrections to the critical exponents that improve the predictions, compared to previous one parameter analyses. We also observe families of compact regulators that rapidly converge towards an optimal functional form as a small number of parameters is progressively introduced.
summary: This paper advances the application of the Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) by introducing a multi-parameter optimization scheme to address the regulator dependence inherent in the theory. Using the 3D Ising model, the authors systematically minimize this dependence by optimizing the regulator shape, leading to improved predictions for critical exponents. This work provides a more robust theoretical framework for calculating critical behavior in statistical field theories.
main_problem: The paper investigates how to systematically minimize the dependence of physical observables on the arbitrary choice of the coarse-graining regulator within the Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) framework.
main_result: By employing a multi-parameter optimization approach based on the Principle of Minimal Sensitivity (PMS), the authors find appreciable corrections to critical exponents for the 3D Ising universality class, improving upon previous single-parameter analyses.
method: The core method involves applying the FRG flow equation (Wetterich-Morris equation) truncated via the derivative expansion up to fourth order, and then optimizing the regulator parameters to satisfy stationarity conditions derived from the PMS.
model_or_system: The study is applied to a scalar field theory representing the three-dimensional Ising universality class, which is a canonical model for continuous phase transitions in statistical mechanics.
key_observables:
The anomalous dimension ($\eta$) and critical exponents ($
u$, $\omega$) are the key observables whose regulator dependence is minimized.
important_parameters: The order of the derivative expansion (up to fourth order) and the number of parameters used to define the polynomial regulator are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the approximation that the flow equation can be truncated (e.g., derivative expansion) and assumes that an optimal regulator shape exists within the chosen functional space of compactly supported polynomials.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail the structure of the flow equations and the derivation of boundary terms for various couplings.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the FRG framework, introduces the multi-parameter optimization via PMS, applies this to the 3D Ising model using the derivative expansion, and calculates the resulting flow equations and improved critical exponents.
why_interesting: While focused on critical phenomena, the rigorous mathematical machinery of optimizing flow equations and handling regulator dependence is a powerful, general theoretical tool applicable to any field requiring systematic renormalization group analysis.
